correctness.rationale: For |z|<2 an absolutely convergent geometric expansion gives S(z)=1+sum_j z/(2^j-z). Along z=-x, x in [0,2), F(x)=sum_j x/(2^j+x) is continuous and strictly increasing. F(1)<sum_j 2^-j=1, whereas the EXACT sum of its first six summands at x=3/2 is 65011734/64203755>1. Thus a unique alpha in (1,3/2) satisfies S(-alpha)=0. Its derivative S'( -alpha )=sum_j 2^j/(2^j+alpha)^2>0 so the zero is simple. The inverse Taylor series has a pole at -alpha, radius R<=alpha<3/2, and limsup|b_n|^(1/n)=1/R>2/3. This contradicts b_n=O(2^-n). The packaged exact-rational verifier reproduces the critical certificate and independently checks the ten-term alternating bound and published initial inverse coefficients.

The inspected 2020 follow-up examines direct unitary Euler Bell series and does not imply the negative-zero obstruction for the reciprocal-unitary-Euler Bell series. OEIS records a value at z=1 only. value.rationale: A published explicit open problem about a key coefficient estimate is disproved rigorously, with a six-term rational witness and an unavoidable simple pole. This settles the sign of the answer and supplies a quantified exponential-growth obstruction. It is mathematically motivated by the arithmetic reciprocal-totient problem rather than by an arbitrary evaluated invariant.
